acceptance_criteria.statement: A deterministic local validator accepts a conforming scenario and rejects missing or malformed required scenario fields without launching a model.
A suite can be invoked explicitly on Codex only, and a Copilot run without one of the four allowed reasons is rejected before harness invocation.

At least one durable flat/hierarchical baseline pair uses identical fixture, prompt, and expected behavior; old/new risk-proportional routing is compared when its historical artifacts exist, and unavailable metrics serialize as unknown rather than zero.

The runner refuses or stops before exceeding each configured limit and stops additional model calls after a configured failure threshold or a systemic materialization, plugin-load, schema, or routing failure.

A completed or failed run leaves a parseable durable machine-readable record with all required identity, result, metric, failure, usage, latency, and raw-artifact fields; missing measurements remain explicitly unknown.
The evaluator scores a supplied profile/plugin variant through the same interface regardless of its origin, and no candidate optimizer or optimization loop is added.

The final report names actual suites and available baselines, gives Codex-first commands and allowed Copilot reasons, describes budget/fail-fast rules, records only bounded smoke/evaluation evidence, states limitations and self-improvement readiness, and confirms no massive optimization corpus was run.
A cross-harness validation request is isolated, read-only, has a different target from its origin, and is rejected if the validator attempts recursive delegation or takes development ownership.

specification.intent: Measure behavior, portability, routing differences, and context cost across harnesses without selecting a best model or spending Copilot quota on large repeated corpora.
non_goals: Choosing a best model or ranking models as the product objective.
Implementing SkillOpt, GEPA, a custom optimizer, candidate generation, or a self-evolving harness.
Running a massive repeated benchmark or optimization corpus during this phase.
Completing unrelated tasks in todos/in_progress, migrating unrelated packs, or treating those notes as completed work.
Proving the GitHub App authorization boundary without a known existing repository target.
normalization_notes: Before approval, mapped the source document's mandatory flat-versus-hierarchical baseline and read-only non-recursive cross-harness validation clauses to REQ/AC-COST-3 and REQ/AC-COST-8. This corrects the initial normalization omission; user intent and SPEC revision remain unchanged.
specification.objective: Add a harness-neutral behavioral evaluation layer that uses Codex by default for costly benchmarks, enforces explicit budgets and justified Copilot usage, persists machine-readable results, and supports matched baseline comparisons for future profile optimizers.

requirements.rationale: Keep scenario intent reusable across harnesses and make routing and conformance observations explicit.
requirements.statement: The evaluation system accepts harness-neutral behavioral scenarios with stable IDs, category, fixture and base revision, prompt, expected behavior, required, forbidden, optional, and metrics fields.

requirements.rationale: Codex has the larger available evaluation budget, while Copilot usage is scarce.
requirements.statement: Costly benchmarks and optimization experiments use Codex by default; Copilot runs require an explicit allowed reason: copilot_specific_behavior, portability_sample, regression_confirmation, or host_specific_agent_behavior.

requirements.rationale: Make baseline comparisons interpretable without inventing evidence or conflating unknown with zero.
requirements.statement: The system creates matched baselines for flat versus hierarchical skills and supports old versus risk-proportional routing comparisons when the historical artifacts exist; comparisons use the same fixture, prompt, and expected behavior, and unavailable metrics remain unknown.

requirements.rationale: Bound cost and stop doomed runs before they consume model quota.
requirements.statement: Evaluation runs support explicit maximum runs, model calls, known tokens, and failures before stop, and fail fast on broken materialization, plugin loading, schemas, or systematic routing failures.

requirements.rationale: Keep evaluation evidence usable by later analysis and candidate optimizers.
requirements.statement: Every evaluation run produces a durable machine-readable artifact containing suite, harness, model, base revision, plugin profile, results, metrics, failures, token usage, latency, and raw artifact references.

requirements.rationale: Separate candidate generation from scoring so future optimizers can reuse the evaluator.
requirements.statement: Evaluation accepts a plugin/profile variant independently of how that variant was generated, without implementing SkillOpt, GEPA, or another optimizer in this phase.

requirements.rationale: Make the phase boundary and evidence available for the next decision.
requirements.statement: The phase report identifies implemented suites, available baselines, Codex-first commands, justified Copilot use, budget rules, bounded smoke/evaluation results, limitations, and what is ready for self-improvement.

requirements.rationale: Detect harness-specific assumptions while preserving ownership and bounding validation depth.
requirements.statement: When a harness-specific change needs validation on another harness, the system supports isolated read-only cross-harness validation; the validator is not the development owner and cannot recursively delegate.
